_how_to_add: One entry per term, any week. Fields: term, meaning (one plain sentence or two), topic (reuse an existing one if it fits), week (the week the term is first taught). The site sorts A-Z itself. Set lesson to the id of the course lesson that explains the word (an item id in that week's content file).

terms.meaning: Success codes. 201 means a new row was saved; 200 means it worked.
401 no or bad token; 403 signed in but not allowed; 404 no such thing (this site also says 404 to hide teacher pages); 422 the body failed the check.
Application Programming Interface: a list of doors (addresses) a program opens so other programs can ask it for things. This site's API lives at fde-learnings.onrender.com/api/fde.
Proving who you are, for example signing in with Google.
What you are allowed to do once you are known. A learner can read announcements; only a teacher can add one.
The header that carries your token: Authorization: Bearer <token>.
The part of an app that runs on a server: it checks requests, does the work and talks to the database. Here: the FastAPI code in backend/.
The start of every address an API uses, such as https://fde-learnings.onrender.com/api/fde. Each route adds its own path after it.
A token you send in the Authorization header. Whoever holds (bears) it is treated as you, so keep it private.
The data sent with a request or a reply, usually JSON. POST, PUT and PATCH carry a body; GET and DELETE usually don't.
Whoever sends the request: a browser, curl, Postman or another server.
One kind of fact in a table, such as title or created_at. Every row has a value for each column.
The moment changes are saved for good. Until db.commit() runs, nothing is really written.
A browser rule: a page may only call an API that lists the page's address as allowed. Set by CORS_ORIGINS on the API.
Create, Read, Update, Delete: the four things you can do with stored data. They map to POST, GET, PUT or PATCH, and DELETE.
A command-line tool that sends one HTTP request and prints the reply. Same job as Postman, but typed.
A program that stores data safely and lets you search it. Here: Postgres on Neon online, a SQLite file on your laptop.
HTTP method that removes something. The D in CRUD.
Putting your code on a host so it runs on a public address instead of only your laptop.
The browser's built-in tools (right-click, Inspect). The Network tab shows every API call the page makes.
One door of an API: a method plus a path, such as POST /teacher/announcements.
A setting given to a program from outside its code, such as DATABASE_URL. Keys live here, never in code.
The Python framework this site's backend is written in. You write a function and mark it with @router.get or @router.post.
A column that points at a row in another table, such as created_by pointing at fde_users.id.
What people see and click: the React page, served by Vercel.
HTTP method that reads. It should never change data. The R in CRUD.
A small labelled detail sent with a request or reply, such as Content-Type: application/json or Authorization.
A company whose computers run your code: Render (API), Vercel (page), Neon (database), LiveKit Cloud (voice bot).
The language browsers and servers use to talk: a request goes out, a reply comes back. HTTPS is the same, encrypted.
The verb of a request: GET, POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE.
A column whose value is unique for each row, so one row can be found exactly. The database picks it on insert.
The four SQL commands behind CRUD. SQLAlchemy writes them for you.
When the caller speaks over the bot. With interruptions on, the bot stops talking and listens.
A plain-text way to write data: {"title": "Hello", "pinned": false}. APIs send and receive it.
JSON Web Token: the signed token this site gives you when you sign in. The API checks the signature on every request.
Large Language Model: the brain of a voice bot that writes the reply text.
Your own computer. http://localhost:8000 only works on your laptop.
A small store inside the browser. This site keeps your token there under the key fde.token.
Object-Relational Mapper: lets you work with rows as Python objects. This site uses SQLAlchemy.
HTTP method that changes part of something that already exists. The U in CRUD.
The part of the URL after the host, such as /api/fde/weeks/week-01.
A value written inside the path, such as week-01 in /weeks/{week_id}. It picks which thing you mean.
Another word for the body.
HTTP method that creates something new. The C in CRUD. A good API replies 201 Created.
A popular SQL database. Neon runs it for this site.
An app for sending API requests with buttons instead of typing curl.
HTTP method that sets something to a given value, creating it if missing. The U in CRUD.
The Python library FastAPI uses to check a request body. A missing or wrong field gets a 422 reply.
Extra options after a ? in the URL, such as ?week_id=week-02. Used to filter or sort, mostly with GET.
What the client sends: method, URL, headers and maybe a body.
What the server sends back: a status code, headers and usually a body.
A common style of API: things are nouns in the path (/announcements) and the method says what to do with them.
The part of FastAPI that matches a method and path to the Python function that handles it.
One record in a table, such as one announcement.
The shape data must have: which fields, which types, which are required.
A computer (or program) that waits for requests and answers them. Uvicorn is the server program here; Render's computer runs it.
A running program that does one job for others. On Render, this API is a 'web service'. LiveKit is a voice service.
In bigger apps, the code between the route and the database that holds the business rules. This site is small, so most routes talk to the database themselves.
One conversation with the database inside one request. get_db() opens it and closes it after the reply.
Structured Query Language: the language databases understand, such as SELECT * FROM fde_announcements.
The Python library (an ORM) this site uses to talk to the database.
A database that is a single file. Used on your laptop when DATABASE_URL is blank.
The 3-digit number at the top of a reply. 2xx worked, 4xx your request is wrong, 5xx the server broke.
Speech-to-text: the ears of a voice bot.
A grid of rows and columns, like one sheet in Excel. This site's tables start with fde_, such as fde_announcements.
A string that proves you are signed in. Send it in the Authorization header.
Text-to-speech: the mouth of a voice bot.
How a voice bot decides you have finished speaking. Wait too little and it cuts you off; too long and it feels slow.
A full web address: https:// + host + path + optional ?query.
The program that runs the FastAPI app and listens for HTTP requests.
Voice Activity Detection: spots when someone is speaking at all. This site's bot uses Silero VAD.
An API call one server makes to another when something happens, such as 'the call ended'. Week 3 joins P1 and P2 this way.
